title: The anonymous cloud folder — question explanation
learningObjective: Configure sharing permissions and expiry consistent with data sensitivity
format: 16:9 educational motion-graphics video; narration; separate captions; no autoplay with sound
visualStyle: Deep navy and charcoal; restrained cyan/electric-blue highlights; limited purple accents; clean typography; purposeful, low-motion transitions; accessible contrast.

scenes.name: Scenario setup
scenes.visual: A team shares a folder containing internal project documents through an anonymous link that never expires. The folder is no longer being actively used.
scenes.direction: Show a fictional simulated setting. Use generic UI and no actual organization, brand, user identity, credential, real URL or live account.

scenes.name: Learning objective and risk cue
scenes.visual: Configure sharing permissions and expiry consistent with data sensitivity
scenes.direction: Highlight only observable cues and explain the decision context without implying certainty beyond the scenario.

scenes.name: Recommended response
scenes.visual: Option A: Restrict access to named authorized accounts, set an expiry/review date and remove obsolete access. Restrict identities and duration, and review existing permissions according to data sensitivity.
scenes.direction: Animate the recommended defensive choice as a clear decision path. Display the action verb and trusted channel/control.

scenes.name: Why the other options fail
scenes.visual: Option B: A folder name does not change who can access its content. Option C: Wider distribution increases exposure and does not establish authorization. Option D: Convenience does not justify indefinite anonymous access.
scenes.direction: Show each unsafe alternative separately with a complete, concise reason. Do not depict operational exploitation, malicious code or credential capture.

scenes.name: Defensive takeaway
scenes.visual: Remove anonymous access, grant only necessary users or groups, set expiry where available and periodically review permissions. Cloud sharing should be identity-bound, least-privilege and time-limited when appropriate.
scenes.direction: Close with one readable takeaway and the next safe action. Keep the final frame long enough for comprehension.
scenes.onScreenText: Cloud sharing should be identity-bound, least-privilege and time-limited when appropriate.

narration: Scenario: A team shares a folder containing internal project documents through an anonymous link that never expires. The folder is no longer being actively used. Safest response: Option A: Restrict access to named authorized accounts, set an expiry/review date and remove obsolete access. Restrict identities and duration, and review existing permissions according to data sensitivity. Option B is unsafe because A folder name does not change who can access its content. Option C is unsafe because Wider distribution increases exposure and does not establish authorization. Option D is unsafe because Convenience does not justify indefinite anonymous access. In practice: Remove anonymous access, grant only necessary users or groups, set expiry where available and periodically review permissions. Key takeaway: Cloud sharing should be identity-bound, least-privilege and time-limited when appropriate.
